answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24h notice? Conditions?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding with water on electrics, in a flat whose tenant is away and unreachable, is a genuine emergency. Conditions: entry only to isolate water and make safe (stopcock under kitchen sink), using the office/out-of-hours key with a witness, keep a record of times and photos, tell the tenant and landlord straight away, and do no more than needed.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (not our tenant)?
answers.answer: Tell her to keep clear of the wet area, turn off the power to her kitchen lights/circuit at the consumer unit if safe to do so, and call 999 if there is any danger, sparking or serious flooding. Tell her we are sending a plumber tonight to stop the water. Don't give out the tenant's number or any tenant details (data protection); we will pass her contact details to the tenant on request. Tell her liability is not decided, so we cannot give a written promise to pay. Suggest she tell her own contents/home insurer and note the damage with photos; the landlord's insurer will be contacted.

answers.question: What actions and notifications, and what must be avoided?
answers.answer: Done: ticket JOB-101 (emergency), Swift assigned, tenant SMS and voicemail attempt logged, landlord emailed, P1 escalation. Avoid: admitting liability or promising to pay, giving the tenant's number or personal details, saying the tenant is away, speculating on the cause, and any commitment on dates or costs.

conflicts: Tenant note says away 9-12 Oct, but the neighbour says nobody is answering; consistent, so not a conflict. Entry assumed unoccupied.

next_actions.action: Assigned Swift Plumbing (out of hours) for tonight's emergency make-safe
SMS tenant explaining emergency entry and make-safe
Emailed landlord about leak and make-safe, no liability accepted
P1 escalation for key-holder entry and neighbour claim

boundaries: Assigning the plumber does not confirm the cause of the leak or who is liable
Nothing said to the neighbour admits liability or promises payment
Entry is limited to make-safe; no other work or inspection of the tenant's belongings
remaining_work: Human/key holder to attend with Swift and enter Flat 4, record entry, isolate water
Confirm Swift attendance and outcome; record work result
Landlord to refer Flat 3's claim to buildings insurer
Tenant to be updated once reachable; give her the 24h-notice-exempt entry record
Follow-up on drying out and repairs, quote approval if over £300 (call Ben first)
details.summary: Neighbour reported an active leak onto a light fitting from Flat 4, whose tenant is away and unreachable. Created emergency ticket JOB-101, assigned Swift Plumbing tonight, informed tenant and landlord, and escalated P1 for key-holder entry and the neighbour's liability demand.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24h notice? Conditions?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding with water on electrics, in a flat whose tenant is away and unreachable, is a genuine emergency. Conditions: entry only to isolate water and make safe (stopcock under kitchen sink), using the office/out-of-hours key with a witness, keep a record of times and photos, tell the tenant and landlord straight away, and do no more than needed.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (not our tenant)?
answers.answer: Tell her to keep clear of the wet area, turn off the power to her kitchen lights/circuit at the consumer unit if safe to do so, and call 999 if there is any danger, sparking or serious flooding. Tell her we are sending a plumber tonight to stop the water. Don't give out the tenant's number or any tenant details (data protection); we will pass her contact details to the tenant on request. Tell her liability is not decided, so we cannot give a written promise to pay. Suggest she tell her own contents/home insurer and note the damage with photos; the landlord's insurer will be contacted.

answers.question: What actions and notifications, and what must be avoided?
answers.answer: Done: ticket JOB-101 (emergency), Swift assigned, tenant SMS and voicemail attempt logged, landlord emailed, P1 escalation. Avoid: admitting liability or promising to pay, giving the tenant's number or personal details, saying the tenant is away, speculating on the cause, and any commitment on dates or costs.

conflicts: Tenant note says away 9-12 Oct, but the neighbour says nobody is answering; consistent, so not a conflict. Entry assumed unoccupied.
assumptions: The call transcript ended after the caller's three statements, so the advice to the caller is described here rather than sent. No channel or number for her is on file.
The out-of-hours key holder is available and Swift will attend in the window; not yet confirmed.
